Fields and schemas

Source: R/schema.R
schema.Rd

schema() builds a schema from named fields, each a type such as int32, decimal(18, 4) or list(string), or the fields made by field() and not_null(). Called with one unnamed argument it returns the schema of that table instead: a data frame's is inferred from its columns.

Usage

schema(..., .metadata = NULL)

field(type, nullable = TRUE, metadata = NULL)

not_null(type)

Arguments

...

Named fields, or one table.

.metadata

Table metadata, a named character vector.

type

A type, as in schema().

nullable

Whether the field may hold NA.

metadata

Field metadata, a named character vector.

Value

schema() a zutable_schema; field() and not_null() a zutable_field.

Details

Type names are read only inside these functions (and na()); they are not R objects. A string is accepted wherever a type is, as is a variable holding a type or a string. The types are:

  • bool, int32, int64, float64, string, date, binary;

  • timestamp(unit, tz), with unit one of "s", "ms", "us" and "ns" and tz a zone name, or NULL for a time without a zone; bare timestamp is timestamp("us", "UTC");

  • decimal(precision, scale), enum(levels), list(type), struct(name = type, ...);

  • r_class("cls"), any S3 vector held as it is, and extension(name), a class registered with register_extension_type().

int8, int16 and float32 read as int32 and float64, which is exact. int64 needs the 'zuint' package, decimal the 'decimal' package, and timestamp("ns") the 'zutempo' package; without them the type is a zutable_type_error.

A POSIXct with no time zone is an instant shown in local time, and is typed timestamp("us", "UTC"), so the type of a vector never depends on the session (design D38).

Examples

s <- schema(
  id   = not_null(int32),
  px   = field(float64, metadata = c(unit = "USD")),
  day  = date,
  tags = list(string)
)
s
#> <zutable_schema> 4 fields
#>   id not_null(int32)
#>   px float64
#>     unit: USD
#>   day date
#>   tags list(string)
schema(data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c("a", "b", "c")))
#> <zutable_schema> 2 fields
#>   x int32
#>   y string
